LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Writing 3.6 Guided Writing: Handwriting (2 sessions) • Vocabulary building • Wor
Topic 3.7: Guided Writing: Creative Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Writing: Creative Writing, part of Writing 3.6 Guided Writing: Handwriting (2 sessions) • Vocabulary building • Wor in Grade 4 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why do you take care of your body? 2. How do poems enhance creativity?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. list vocabulary related to the theme in neat and legible handwriting,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. re-write a simple poem based on the theme for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. develop interest in artistic expression through writing.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. list vocabulary related to the theme in neat and legible handwriting,

   Guided Writing: Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. re-write a simple poem based on the theme for comprehension,

   Guided Writing: Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. develop interest in artistic expression through writing.

   Guided Writing: Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. list the parts of the body on flashcards to form a vocabulary bank on words acquired,

2. draw and colour the various parts of the body,

3. organise the drawings in the class portfolio,

4. use think-pair-share strategy to write simple sentences about parts of the body,

5. work jointly with peers to re- write a simple poem (one stanza long) based on the theme,

6. stage the poem during interclass festivals or school functions. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. list the parts of the body on flashcards to form a vocabulary bank on words acquired,
2. draw and colour the various parts of the body,
3. organise the drawings in the class portfolio,
4. use think-pair-share strategy to write simple sentences about parts of the body,
5. work jointly with peers to re- write a simple poem (one stanza long) based on the theme,
6. stage the poem during interclass festivals or school functions. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Writing: Creative Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical thinking and problem solving: This is developed as learners use think-pair-share strategy to write simple sentences

about parts of the body.

Values:
Unity: This is enhanced as the learner works jointly with peers to re-write a simple poem (one stanza long) based on the theme.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Health promotion (self-awareness) : This is addressed as the learner appreciates parts of the body and the various functions they

serve.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner is able to link the concept of composing poems to their learning of similar performance concepts in Creative Arts.
